sample_unit: real clinical cases (each queried three times per LLM; compared with 78 pediatric clinicians)

links.outcome: Human-AI complementarity: union accuracy of clinicians plus LLM versus clinicians alone
links.effect: Union accuracy with o1-preview was 94.3%, a 10-percentage-point uplift over clinicians alone.
links.quote: Human-Artificial intelligence complementarity analysis revealed 94.3% union accuracy with o1-preview, representing a 10-percentage-point uplift over clinicians alone.

links.outcome: Top-1 diagnostic accuracy of LLMs compared with pediatric clinicians on the same cases
links.effect: o1-preview and Claude-3.5 Sonnet achieved mean Top-1 accuracies of 60.0% and 59.0% versus clinicians' 48.2% (ORs 2.99 and 2.75, both P < 0.001).
links.quote: o1-preview and Claude-3.5 Sonnet achieved mean Top-1 accuracies of 60.0% and 59.0%, respectively, compared to clinicians' 48.2% (odds ratios [ORs]: 2.99 and 2.75, both P < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic performance and usability of multiple LLMs compared to clinicians using retrospective real-world pediatric clinical cases, but does not test a specific operational guardrail or deployment practice.
